correctness.rationale: For every dimension and time, the stopped-Poisson transition kernel differentiates to p_{k-1}-p_k, and row/column sign telescoping gives the exact norms. The infinity time optimizer follows piecewise t p_k monotonicity and Stirling. The unique maximum of t F is certified analytically by a strictly decreasing ratio F/(t p_{n-1}); the alternative columns have O(sqrt(n)) time-weighted bounds. Stirling at n-c sqrt(n log n) and a geometric Poisson tail prove both the optimizer location and sharp L1 boundary layer. A standalone checker independently compared finite matrix exponentials to both formulas.

value.rationale: The norm of a time derivative is a natural sharp analyticity/smoothing stability invariant for finite positive semigroups. This explicit absorbing family has the same two spectral points in every dimension and uniformly bounded generator matrix entries, yet its sharp l-infinity constant grows only as sqrt(n), while its l1 constant grows nearly linearly; the latter has a nontrivial optimized moderate-deviation shift sqrt(n log n). This is a structural limitation of predicting endpoint sensitivity from spectral location or from row contraction, not an arbitrary finite-table recomputation.
